text:
maria: quick heads-up — vendor posted patch for CVE-2025-4412 (openssl client-side cert parsing). appears exploitable in our KMS client library. can we do a fast triage? :eyes:
jonathan: on it. do we have telemetry on which stacks call our KMS client directly (hosted api vs dedicated vs private)?
li: looking now. short summary: CVSS 8.1, remote code potential via crafted cert chain on client handshake. our usages: 1) hosted control-plane -> vendor KMS (most calls in control plane services), 2) dedicated customer nodes call our kms-proxy for envelope ops, 3) private on-prem may have their own kms. exposure varies by deployment.
srebot: automated scan: 1749456801 — 42 containers using openssl < 3.0.8 detected in prod-control-plane (non-data-plane). flagged images: infra/keyring-manager:v2.4.1, kms-proxy:v1.8.2.
emma: customer-success: any immediate customer-facing impact? enterprise customers expecting SLA for Dedicated. windows/timing matter.
product-security: quick decision matrix we need: exploitability, likely public exploit, SLA risk if we pause traffic, and whether to force KMS key rotation. thoughts?
maria: exploitability looks realistic against our KMS client path (control-plane calls). unlikely to leak plaintext keys without additional auth, but could run arbitrary code in control-plane pod. that threatens control-plane integrity and could cause config leaks. treat as high-priority for hosted/Dedicated-control-plane.
jonathan: propose staged plan: 1) emergency patch for hosted control-plane images (hot rebuild + redeploy canary) 2) Dedicated — schedule rolling patch in off-peak per customer tier (tier-1 immediate canary + 24h staged), 3) Private — notify customers with mitigation guidance and backport patch artifacts.
li: technical note — patching openssl requires building against 3.0.8 ABI changes. kms-proxy v1.8.2 has dynamic TLS stacks; hot-restart works but we need to rotate sidecars in correct order: update keyring-manager -> kms-proxy -> control-plane-api. minimal disruption if we drain connections first. include command snippet for canary rollout:

```bash
# example canary deploy for hosted control-plane
kubectl set image deploy/keyring-manager keyring-manager=infra/keyring-manager:v2.4.2-canary -n control-plane
kubectl rollout status deploy/keyring-manager -n control-plane
# wait 10m, check metrics/logs, then continue
```

product-security: SLA considerations: Hosted API customers on free/standard tiers — do immediate patch, no maintenance window notice required. Dedicated tier-1 (contracted SLA) — need 48h notice for planned maintenance if we expect any potential 99.9 latency hits. But for security hotfix we can apply as emergency maintenance under contract clause; coordinate with account teams.
emma: i'll assemble a short customer advisory for Dedicated customers explaining emergency patch, expected impact: up to 2m rolling restarts per node, possible transient 429s. ask sales to notify top 10 customers.
jonathan: public exposure? haven't seen PoC in the wild. vendor says no known exploit yet. still assume high probability. recommend we treat as ~TLP:AMBER for internal comms.
maria: KMS key rotation: forcing rotation is heavy and will break Dedicated/private customers who bring their own keys. suggestion: do not force rotate global keys, but add a flag in the patch to log any cert-chain anomalies and emit audit events to detect exploitation attempts. if we see anomalous auths, escalate to rotation.
li: agree. we can add extra audit fields in kms-proxy: add "tls_cert_chain_hash" and immediate alert rule. quick config diff:

```json
{"log_level":"info","tls_extra_audit":true}
```

maria: timeline proposal: immediate canary on hosted in next 2 hours, roll to hosted fully within 6 hours if no anomalies, Dedicated tier-1 canary within 12 hours, full Dedicated roll within 36 hours, Private patch artifacts + advisory within 24 hours.
product-security: assign owners: maria -> hosted rollout, jonathan -> Dedicated schedule + account comms, emma -> customer advisory, li -> patch PR + audit fields, sec-oncall -> monitoring + pager rules.
jonathan: also flag release for eng-sre channel with short runbook. include rollback steps: revert image and re-route traffic to fallback region if any instability.
srebot: deploy-bot: created ticket INF-4721 with priority P1, link: https://issues.internal/INF-4721
maria: ok, i'll start the canary build now and ping when logs look clean. thanks all. :thumbsup:
emma: noted, prepping customer note draft.
product-security: keep me posted, we'll prepare a legal/comms blurb in case this is public.
jonathan: one more: for Dedicated customers with strict maintenance windows, include an opt-in 'accelerated hotfix' clause next time in contract templates.
maria: agreed. end plan for now. will update thread with canary results.
